utterances.text: Perhaps to avoid whatever mistake, put a yellow sticker anyhow on the front page. Mr. Q, just to make sure whenever your name might appear, that no one can see it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Would you quickly have a look at the photographs in that folder. Please have a look at the photographs. Are these the photographs you took of the scene of the 21st -- scene of the events of the 21st of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There is some typescript -- I beg your pardon --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please switch on your microphone, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The events which I refer to are the events of the 22nd of January 1994. These pictures are the pictures from that event? Are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, there is some typescript below these photographs. Who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please have a look at the photographs on page 1. I don't know if it could be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, could you put it on the ELMO so that you can either look to your right, Mr. Q, when you see the photograph or look on your screen where it also appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In that picture, do you see snow on the ground?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What was the weather like that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: It was fairly cloudy, but there was no precipitation. It was perhaps a little warmer, as far as I can remember, compared to the days during which it snowed. That is why I consider it to have been a bit warmer then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if there was any shelling in the area before the set of shells that you investigated fell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: I am sure that in this area there was no shelling for 26 days. So after a pause of 20 -- of 20 days, these two shells fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From your investigation, did you receive information as to what the children who died and were injured were doing at the time of the shelling?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: At that time, all the children were possibly playing in the snow and this can be seen because of the sleigh. They were probably playing in the snow which had fallen in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Now the photograph at page number 1 shows the explosion inside number 3 Cetiniska Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, is this the number 1 that we have on the screen or is it a different photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you, Mr. Usher, move the photo so we can see what number. It is number one, yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From your typewritten note here, this photograph shows explosion inside number 3 Cetiniska Street. That is correct, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the photograph; do you see an arrow in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What is that arrow pointing to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: The arrow is pointing to the site of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could you have a look at photograph number 2, please. That, from your note, is the site of the explosion of the previous -- the site of the explosion shown in the proceeding photograph, but from another angle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, if you find a suitable moment either now or within one or two minutes to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the arrow also points to the impact site; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS Q
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If it pleases the Court, perhaps I could take it now. It might give me an opportunity to work on the use of the microphone in these circumstances, which is really distracting me at this point in time. Perhaps this might be a convenient time for the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Q, it is 7.00, so we stop for today. This court resumes tomorrow at a quarter past 2.00, but I think you will not be called right at a quarter past 2.00. We have to deal with one or two other issues first and that may take 15 to 30 minutes. I know sometimes you have to wait here to see whether you will be called or not. We apologise for that. But I can't change it at this very moment. So we will adjourn until tomorrow in the afternoon, same courtroom, at a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 7.00, p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th, day of April, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
